page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It includes 1890 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is also strong in Geekbench, though stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests register in the average tier. Memory performance is notable, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, despite raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks falling into the middle 50%. The processor's instruction set, including AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI, supports strong performance in CPU encryption and image processing.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-memory ratio and substantial 1890 GB local storage, the D32ads_v6 is suited for database operations, software compilation, and web serving. It demonstrates strong capabilities in light LLM inference, particularly with smaller 135M models, though performance scales down to average for larger 7B and 70B models. Qualitatively, the instance offers balanced resource density, making it a cost-efficient option for general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring local scratch space and strong single-threaded execution without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.
